new_findings.title: A null-function tail never advances the reconstructed walker.
new_findings.trigger: A linked terminal callback has function == null; its owner object and list links are otherwise valid.
new_findings.counterexample: One terminal null-function callback. Retail skips to the cached null successor and returns zero. Source leaves node unchanged and revisits the same callback.
new_findings.observable_effect: Nontermination of the selected scheduler pass for this valid null-function branch.
new_findings.root_cause: The null-function arm updates node only through next->previous; with no next it keeps the predecessor.
new_findings.correction: Walk a cached successor as the retail code does. A null function must advance without incrementing the count.
new_findings.positive_control: A normal linked callback and a nonterminal null-function callback should not stall.
new_findings.finding_basis: Source and original reference control/data flow; synthetic host execution is corroboration only.
new_findings.valid_input_domain: A linked terminal callback has function == null; its owner object and list links are otherwise valid. List nodes and callback owner pointers must be valid; system-lock behavior and concurrent mutation are outside the probe.
remaining_assumptions: The specific triggering callback state/return value has not been observed in a live retail gameplay window.

new_findings.title: Retiring a tail callback restarts traversal and repeats earlier work.
new_findings.trigger: A surviving callback A is followed by a terminal callback B that returns zero.
new_findings.counterexample: A returns one; B returns zero. Retail executes A,B once and returns count two. Source restarts from the sentinel after B's removal, executes A again, and returns count three.
new_findings.observable_effect: Extra update or draw callback execution in one scheduler pass, and a wrong count.
new_findings.root_cause: The result-zero branch substitutes the list sentinel when its saved successor is null.
new_findings.correction: Continue at the cached next node, including null meaning end-of-list; do not turn ordinary tail removal into restart.
new_findings.positive_control: Two surviving callbacks execute once each and return two.

new_findings.title: The secondary walker inherits primary-only meanings for return codes six and seven.

new_findings.title: Unowned callback removal clears the owner instead of the function.
new_findings.trigger: Remove a linked non-owning callback, with deletion bit one clear.
new_findings.counterexample: Retail unlinks and clears the function at +8 while preserving owner at +0x20. Source unlinks, zeroes owner, and leaves function nonnull.
new_findings.observable_effect: The retained callback object's observable state is wrong; later reuse observes a lost owner and an uncleared function.
new_findings.root_cause: Unconditional teardown writes target the wrong field; function clearing is restricted to the freeing branch.
new_findings.correction: Clear function unconditionally after valid unlinking and preserve owner as retail does. Separately preserve the original guard against unlinking a sentinel.
new_findings.positive_control: An unlinked callback is not removed again, and owned nodes are retired exactly once.
new_findings.finding_basis: Source and original reference control/data flow; synthetic host execution is corroboration only.
